subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK and command-cron paths, and what owner/security gates are required?
rationale: The remaining work can expose filesystem, process, session, cron, Gateway, and node actions without an LLM turn, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product boundary or security gate shape.

options.title: Keep the umbrella and land narrow gated slices
options.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active host-FS and readiness PRs, requiring explicit owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Limit support to shipped direct-invoke paths
options.body: Declare HTTP/RPC/SDK and command cron sufficient for now, and reject broader host-FS, exec, slash, and CLI direct dispatch until a maintainer sponsors a narrower proposal.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Allow broader direct tool execution only with a named security design, upgrade proof, and operator-facing controls that make the risk explicit.

recommendation.title: Keep the umbrella and land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active host-FS and readiness PRs, requiring explicit owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily the dangerous-tool and owner-gated Gateway security boundary, and recent history ties steipete to that boundary.
